results.title: Strategies to Support Successful Translation of Preclinical Biomarker Assays
results.content: # Strategies to Support Successful Translation of Preclinical Biomarker Assays. Together, these pillars enable a precision medicine-based approach for successfully addressing complex, immune-driven diseases through the development and applications of biomarkers to support clinical development. Biomarker-driven strategies have been shown to increase the likelihood of drug approval by approximately 40 percent, which represents both significant patient benefit and potential cost savings.1 To adopt these strategies, clinical design and execution must be fully integrated with a clear biomarker-informed development plan. ## Transitioning from Preclinical to Clinical Biomarker Assays. The impact of biomarkers on successful clinical development is increasing. To be clinically useful and practical, biomarkers must correlate with a clinically relevant endpoint and, ideally, the sample collection should be minimally invasive to the patient. Collecting the right sample type and processing it in the right way for the specific clinical biomarker assay is imperative for generating high quality, actionable data. * Where biomarker data are used to inform clinical decision-making, appropriate assay validation, perhaps to CLIA, becomes necessary. Preclinical and clinical biomarker teams must work closely together to develop a sound clinical biomarker strategy. Discussion and decisions on assay options, feasibility, development, and validation should occur before clinical collections plans are finalized to avoid having to change study protocols. It is vital that both preclinical and clinical samples are of the utmost quality and suitability for the biomarker assay required. In addition to animal models, preclinical human tissue samples are essential for assay development, assay validation, biomarker validation, and clinical proof of concept. Typically, there will be many patients, multiple timepoints, and diverse sample formats required for the various downstream biomarker assays required, which may be run at different analytical labs. Given this multifaceted complexity, it is critical to have clear procedures and training in place to ensure that collection, processing, logistics, timing of shipping, sample storage, and assay execution are carefully choreographed. Maintaining engagement between discovery and clinical biomarker and operations teams enables better understanding and planning for translation of preclinical assays to the clinical operations environment. As a full service CRO, we bring expertise throughout the development process, from study design and execution services to specialty laboratory, sample logistics, biomarker data management, and regulatory and market access capabilities.

Digital technologies capable of detecting biomarkers and their subtle fluctuations at ultra-low concentrations, far beyond the limits of conventional methods, are transforming biomedical research. By enabling detection of proteins and nucleic acids at the single-molecule level, Simoa® technology has redefined sensitivity and precision in biomarker analysis, driving major advances in our understanding of human health and disease. The Simoa ultra-sensitive biomarker detection platform has powered over 3,200 peer-reviewed publications across diverse areas such as neurology, immunology, oncology, cardiology, and infectious disease. To make Simoa’s ultra-sensitive detection accessible to a wider research community, Quanterix offers a complete suite of solutions, including assay kits, a flexible instrument portfolio, and contract lab services, tailored to a range of scientific needs and budgets. Our core platforms: the fully automated Simoa HD-X Analyzer® and the compact, semi-automated Quanterix SR-X® Biomarker Detection System, are powered by our proprietary bead-based Simoa technology. #### **Quanterix SR-X Biomarker Detection System: Affordable, Flexible, Ultra-Sensitive Detection at Your Fingertips**. The SR-X is an ideal entry point into ultra-sensitive biomarker detection. It offers the same ultra-sensitivity as the HD-X, with flexibility for custom assay development using the Simoa Homebrew solution while requiring less sample volume, perfect for studies where sample availability is limited. The SR-X supports both single- and multiplex detection of low-abundance biomarkers across various sample types. It can detect up to four biomarkers simultaneously from very small sample volumes, making it an excellent fit for research studies with limited or precious samples. As an accessible benchtop system, the SR-X has opened new doors to researchers around the world. #### **Unlock Big Discoveries with the Quanterix SR-X Biomarker Detection System**. The SR-X delivers Simoa’s powerful single-molecule detection capabilities in a compact, cost-effective benchtop format.
